title: Jason and the One Sandal

scope.description: Jason's displacement, upbringing by Chiron, return to Iolcus, aid to disguised Juno, and Pelias' recognition of the one-sandaled man.
scope.boundaryRationale: The unit excludes source headings and the later Phryxus/Helle banquet tale, ending with Pelias' oracle recognition.

sourceBoundaryDecision: The unit excludes source headings and the later Phryxus/Helle banquet tale, ending with Pelias' oracle recognition.

evidence.sourceText: Æson and Alcimede, in fear of their lives, were forced to resort to a hasty and secret flight, taking with them their only son, Jason.
Their happiness, however, was soon disturbed by Pelias, the king's brother, who, aided by an armed host, took forcible possession of the throne.
At Iolcus, in Thessaly, there once reigned a virtuous king, Æson, with his good wife, Alcimede.
evidence.coreferenceNote: Source uses the ligature form Æson; this note avoids ASCII word-boundary false negatives.

evidence.sourceText: At Iolcus, in Thessaly, there once reigned a virtuous king, Æson, with his good wife, Alcimede.

The king and queen soon found a place of refuge, but, afraid lest their hiding place should be discovered and they should all be slain by the cruel Pelias, they intrusted their son to the Centaur Chiron, revealing to him alone the secret of the child's birth, and bidding him train him up to avenge their wrongs.

He was about to part from the old dame with a kindly farewell, when she was suddenly transformed into a large, handsome, imperious-looking woman, whom, owing to the peacock by her side, he immediately recognized as Juno, queen of heaven.
At Iolcus, in Thessaly, there once reigned a virtuous king, Æson, with his good wife, Alcimede.

After many an effort, breathless and almost exhausted, Jason reached the opposite bank, and, after depositing his burden there, scrambled up beside her, casting a rueful glance at the torrent, which had wrenched off one of his golden sandals.

narrative.synopsis: Pelias usurps Aeson's throne, Jason is hidden with Chiron, Juno tests him at a stream, and Pelias recognizes the oracle's warning when Jason returns with one sandal.
narrative.openingSituation: Pelias has seized Aeson's throne in Iolcus.
narrative.centralConflict: Jason returns as the dispossessed heir whose appearance threatens Pelias.
narrative.resolution: Pelias sees Jason's bare foot and remembers the oracle.
narrative.outcome: Jason confronts Pelias and demands his father's throne.
storyline: Pelias seized Aeson's throne at Iolcus.
Aeson and Alcimede entrusted Jason to Chiron.
Jason lost one golden sandal while carrying disguised Juno across the torrent.
Pelias recognized Jason as the one-sandaled man warned of by the oracle.
